chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I cannot reach the Black Stone.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'When you perform the obligatory Tawaf, it will not harm you.'

key_terms.يَخْلُصُ: To reach / to succeed in reaching

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I cannot reach the Black Stone during Tawaf due to crowds?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the physical act of touching or kissing the Black Stone is not a strict condition for the validity of the obligatory Tawaf, offering relief to pilgrims during periods of intense crowding. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the intention (niyyah) and the circumambulation itself as the core of the ritual, rather than the specific physical contact with the stone. It reflects the principle of ease (yusr) in Islamic jurisprudence, ensuring that the Hajj remains accessible despite logistical challenges.
